asideReason: The Taroko gorge road between Taroko and Tianxiang was still closed when the park's own page was read, with no firm reopening date. Indian visitor visas also sit in a heavier designated-country process. The rest of the island is good. The famous landscape this group would cross the world for was not available.
name: Taiwan
regionLabel: Taipei and the east, with Taroko unresolved
summary: Food, museums, hot springs and forest railways. Held out of the main list because the gorge that would make the trip was closed.
why: If Taroko's gorge section has reopened by 2027 and the Indian visa looks workable, Taiwan becomes a serious family option. Until then it is a note, not a recommendation.
distinctive: A dense, kind, food-centred island with real mountains, currently missing its signature walk.
weather: April is mild and can be wet. Seasonal expectation only.
crowds: Taipei is a working city. Taroko, when open, has busy viewpoints. Not researched as a crowd calendar.
natureExperiences: Alishan or a forest railway if you go without Taroko
Taroko only after the park reopens the gorge road
age6: Taipei museums, night markets in small doses, and short coastal walks.
age12: The science museums are a strength.
age14: The same, plus the food and the train system.
adults: Food and museums. The gorge was the nature reason.
gettingAround: High-speed rail and local trains. Excellent for a group. A car is optional.
meetingPoint: Taipei. Easy hub compared with Paro or the Azores.
visaAu: Australian passports can enter visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism, with a passport valid at least six months and a return ticket, according to the Bureau of Consular Affairs and Smartraveller. A Taiwan Arrival Card is part of the process. Recheck.
visaIn: India is on Taiwan's designated-country list for visitor visas. The Bureau of Consular Affairs describes an extra procedure, including an identity certificate. This is a harder visa than Japan's ordinary tourist visa. Read the current BOCA page before anyone plans around it.
disadvantages: Taroko's Taroko–Tianxiang section, including bus service, was closed with an uncertain reopening after the 2024 earthquake and a later typhoon.
The Indian visa process is heavier than for the other East Asian options.
Without the gorge, the trip is a good city-and-food holiday and a weaker nature holiday.
uncertainties: Whether the gorge road has reopened by April 2027.
